# Apache Juneau

> Apache Juneau is a Java toolkit for marshalling POJOs to and from many formats (JSON, XML, HTML, UON, URL-encoding, MessagePack, RDF, CSV, YAML and more), building REST servers and clients, and writing configurable microservices, built around a common bean-context and annotation model. This index links to the documentation topics, grouped as in the site sidebar.

## Getting Started

- [Getting Started](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/GettingStarted): New to Juneau? Work through these four short pages in order. Each builds on the previous one and takes a few minutes.
- [1. Install Juneau](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/GettingStartedInstall): Juneau requires Java 17+. All modules are published to Maven Central under the group id `org.apache.juneau`.
- [2. Your First Serializer](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/GettingStartedSerializer): With `juneau-marshall` on the classpath, the `Json` marshaller turns a bean into JSON and back in one call.
- [3. Your First REST App](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/GettingStartedRestApp): A Juneau REST resource is a plain class annotated with `@Rest`. Methods annotated with `@RestGet`, `@RestPost`, and friends become endpoints, and return values are serialized according to the...
- [4. Your First Client](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/GettingStartedClient): The REST client calls the service from the previous page and parses the response into the same `Pet` bean.
- [Starter Projects](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/StarterProjects): Apache Juneau provides three minimal, clone-and-go "Hello World" starter projects — one per deployment type. They are deliberately simpler than the petstore showcase: entry-point templates you can...
- [v10.0 Migration Guide](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/V10MigrationGuide): The following guide can be used to help migrate your code to v10.0. Note that you can also refer to the Release Notes for changes as well.

## About Juneau

- [Juneau Ecosystem](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/JuneauEcosystemOverview): Apache Juneau™ is a single cohesive Java ecosystem for marshalling Java objects to a wide variety of data formats and creating annotation-based REST end-to-end server and client APIs.
- [Framework Comparisons](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/FrameworkComparisons): This page describes how Juneau's feature set lines up against a few popular alternatives. Rather than declaring an overall "winner", each table below simply notes whether a given capability is...
- [Why Choose Juneau?](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/WhyJuneau): Apache Juneau™ offers a unique combination of simplicity, power, and zero-dependency design that makes it an excellent choice for modern Java development. Here's why developers choose Juneau over...

- [@BeanType Annotation](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/BeanTypeAnnotation): The @BeanType annotation is applied to classes to control bean introspection and modeling.
- [@BeanProp Annotation](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/BeanPropAnnotation): The @BeanProp annotation is applied to bean fields, getter/setter methods, and constructor parameters to control bean introspection and property modeling.
- [@BeanCtor Annotation](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/BeanCtorAnnotation): The @BeanCtor annotation is applied to bean constructors to map constructor arguments to property names on beans with read-only properties.
- [@BeanIgnore Annotation](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/BeanIgnoreAnnotation): The @BeanIgnore annotation (`org.apache.juneau.commons.bean`) excludes a class, field, method, or constructor from bean introspection — the model-side decision about whether something participates...
- [@NameProperty Annotation](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/NamePropertyAnnotation): The @NameProperty annotation is used to identify a setter method or field for setting the name of a POJO as it's known by its parent object.
- [@ParentProperty Annotation](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/ParentPropertyAnnotation): The @ParentProperty annotation is used to identify a setter method or field for adding a parent reference to a child object.
- [POJO Builders](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/PojoBuilders): Juneau parsers can use builders to instantiate POJOs. This is useful in cases where you want to create beans with read-only properties.

- [Parsing into Generic Models](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/ParsingIntoGenericModels): The Juneau parsers are not limited to parsing back into the original bean classes. If the bean classes are not available on the parsing side, the parser can also be used to parse into a generic...

- [@Html Annotation](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/HtmlAnnotation): The @Html annotation can be used to customize how POJOs are serialized to HTML on a per-class/field/method basis.

- [HtmlDocSerializer](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/HtmlDocSerializer): HtmlDocSerializer is an extension of HtmlSerializer that wraps serialized POJOs in a complete HTML document.
- [BasicHtmlDocTemplate](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/BasicHtmlDocTemplate): The BasicHtmlDocTemplate class defines a default template for HTML documents created by HtmlDocSerializer.

- [OpenAPI Parsers](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/OpenApiParsers): The OpenApiParser class is used to convert HTTP parts back into POJOs.

- [Array-Record Streaming](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/ArrayRecordStreaming): The `readArrayRecords(...)` / `writeArrayRecords(...)` factories — declared by the ArrayRecordReadable / ArrayRecordWritable

## REST

- [juneau-rest](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/JuneauRest): The `juneau-rest` family of modules provides a complete, end-to-end REST stack built on top of the Juneau marshalling APIs. Because both the server and client sides share the same POJO-centric...
- [juneau-rest-common](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/JuneauRestCommon): `juneau-rest-common` ships as two sibling Maven artifacts:
- [Helper Classes](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/HelperClasses): The org.apache.juneau.http.header package contains various convenience classes for creating standard HTTP components using static imports.
- [Annotations](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/Annotations): The org.apache.juneau.http package contains annotations for defining both server and client side APIs.
- [HTTP Headers](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/HttpHeaders): The org.apache.juneau.http.header package contains transport-neutral header beans for all common HTTP headers. These beans implement the HttpHeader interface, which mirrors
- [HTTP Parts](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/HttpParts): The org.apache.juneau.http.part package contains implementations of `org.apache.http.NameValuePair` to be used for query/form-data/path parts and part lists.
- [HTTP Entities and Resources](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/HttpEntitiesAndResources): The org.apache.juneau.http.classic.entity package contains implementations of `org.apache.http.HttpEntity`. These are entities that can be sent or received with an HTTP message.
- [HTTP Responses](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/HttpResponses): The org.apache.juneau.http.response package contains predefined transport-neutral HttpResponseMessage implementations for most standard HTTP responses.
- [Remote Proxy Interfaces](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RemoteProxyInterfaces): The org.apache.juneau.http.remote package contains the annotations used for defining client-side remote proxies.
- [juneau-rest-server](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/JuneauRestServer):

- [Child Resources](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/ChildResources): Child Resources are REST servlets or objects that are linked to parent resources through the @Rest(children) annotation.
- [Path Variables](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/PathVariables): The path can contain variables that get resolved to @Path parameters or access through the RestRequest.getPathParams() method.

- [Lifecycle Hooks](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/LifecycleHooks): Lifecycle hooks allow you to hook into lifecycle events of the servlet/resource creation and REST calls.

- [@RestOp-Annotated Method](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestOpAnnotatedMethods): REST Java methods are identified on REST servlets using the @RestOp annotation.
- [Inferred HTTP Methods and Paths](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/InferredHttpMethodsAndPaths): When the `method` and/or `path` values are not specified, their values are inferred from the Java method name.

- [Java Method Return Types](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/JavaMethodReturnTypes): The return type of the Java method can be any serializable POJO as defined in POJO Categories.

- [Path Patterns](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/PathPatterns): The @RestOp(path) annotation allows you to define URL path patterns to match against. These patterns can contain variables of the form `{xxx}` that can be passed in directly to the Java methods as...
- [Matchers](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/Matchers): RestMatcher is used to allow multiple Java methods to be tied to the same HTTP method and path but differentiated by some request attribute such as a specific header value.
- [Overloading HTTP Methods](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/OverloadingHttpMethods): Through the use of the built-in `method` GET parameter, you can implement requests beyond the basic REST http method types.

- [@Remote](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/Remote): The @Remote annotation is used on your interface class to identify it as a REST proxy interface.
- [@RemoteOp](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RemoteMethod): The @RemoteOp annotation is applied to methods of @Remote-annotated interfaces to identify REST endpoints.
- [@Content](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/Content): The @Content annotation can be applied to arguments of @RemoteOp-annotated methods to denote that they are the HTTP body of the request.
- [@FormData](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/FormData): The @FormData annotation can be applied to arguments of @RemoteOp-annotated methods to denote that they are form-data parameters on the request.
- [@Query](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/Query): The @Query annotation can be applied to arguments of @RemoteOp-annotated methods to denote that they are query parameters on the request.
- [@Header](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/Header): The @Header annotation can be applied to arguments of @RemoteOp-annotated methods to denote that they are header parameters on the request.
- [@Path](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/Path): The @Path annotation can be applied to arguments of @RemoteOp-annotated methods to denote that they are path parameters on the request.
- [@Request](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/Request): The @Request annotation can be applied to a type of a @RemoteOp-annotated method to identify it as a bean for setting HTTP parts through a bean-like interface.
- [@Response](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/Response): The @Response annotation can be applied to types returned by @RemoteOp-annotated methods.

- [NG Requests](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/NgRequests): A request is built fluently from a `RestClient` verb method and executed with `run()`. Each verb (`get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `head`, and `request(method, url)`) returns a `RestRequest`.
- [NG Responses](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/NgResponses): `run()` returns a `RestResponse`. It is `Closeable` and holds the connection until closed, so always use try-with-resources.
- [NG Body Converters](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/NgBodyConverters): A `BodyConverter` turns an object passed to `RestRequest.body(Object)` into a transport body *before* the client falls back to the default serializer.
- [NG Assertions](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/NgAssertions): `RestResponse.assertThat()` returns a `ResponseAssertion` (package `org.apache.juneau.rest.client.assertion`) for fluent checks. Failures throw `AssertionError`, so they work directly in JUnit tests.

## Guides & Reference

- [Security](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/Security): Security is an ongoing concern in any library. Juneau is designed so that its serializers and parsers are safe by default — POJO types are inferred from the `Class` objects you pass in rather than...
- [Marshalling Security](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/MarshallingSecurity): One common security vulnerability is the ability to create arbitrary Java object instances through crafted user input.
- [SVL Security](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/SvlSecurity): Care must be used when defining new Vars using the SVL API since mistakes could potentially expose system properties, environment variables, or even file system files.
- [REST Security](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/RestSecurity): Denial of service attacks can be alleviated through the maxInput() setting.
- [Content Security Policy](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/ContentSecurityPolicy): Content Security Policy (CSP) is a browser security mechanism that lets a server declare which content sources a page may load and execute, mitigating cross-site-scripting (XSS) and data-injection...
- [v9.0 Migration Guide](https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/V9MigrationGuide): The following guide can be used to help migrate your code to v9.0. Note that you can also refer to the Release Notes for changes as well.
